provenance_tree._comment: Ordered rules; first match wins. Conditions reference fact families and provider-census facts produced and recorded by Core through traust pqc prescan.

rules.when: fact paths are vendor-tagged (VENDOR_RX)
zero crypto facts AND portfolio graph shows sidecar/route TLS termination for the product
assessment_basis is sbom-only, or bundle/FBC/image-only repo
KE/SIG/KEYGEN call-site facts in first-party paths, or HP_C_OPENSSL_LOWLEVEL facts
HP_GROUPS_/HP_POLICY_/HP_ENV_ pin facts present
DEP_/HP_FW_ facts only, no first-party algorithm selection
provider facts present; zero pins; zero direct call sites; C tier EVP-only

remediation_effort._comment: Ordered rules; first match wins. Provenance/agility facts do not establish effort size: null means unknown. Canonical sizes are defined by traust-contracts enums/v1/effort.json, with no duration thresholds or legacy-label mapping. Only the first rule establishes external blocking; omitted blocked_external remains unknown. If no rule matches, size remains null and blocking requires separate evidence.

rules.when: provenance in [vendored, externalized] OR (delegated-dependency AND library has no PQC roadmap)
native-first-party AND (AGIL-1 or AGIL-2 or AGIL-6 = no)
delegated-dependency OR (inherited-constrained AND pin facts > 1) OR (native-first-party AND AGIL-3/6 = yes)
inherited-platform OR (inherited-constrained AND pin facts == 1)

readiness_buckets._comment: Plan v1.3 section 4.6; thresholds are calibration knob 5. Evaluate rules in listed order, first match wins, then apply bucket_override. Predicates preserve the original ordered provenance/agility branches, independently of effort size or separately evidenced blocking. Keep the existing dominant-blocking selection and all-clock-items quantifier (including its empty-set behavior); do not introduce new aggregation or fallback rules.

rules.when: zero-hit with coverage assertion, OR sbom-only with all scored checks na
dominant blocking condition is provenance in [vendored, externalized] OR (provenance=delegated-dependency AND library has no PQC roadmap)
overall >= 80 AND no 2030-clock items AND PQCA-1 = yes

overall in [50, 80) OR all clock items satisfy (NOT (provenance in [vendored, externalized] OR (provenance=delegated-dependency AND library has no PQC roadmap)) AND NOT (provenance=native-first-party AND (AGIL-1 or AGIL-2 or AGIL-6 = no)) AND (provenance=delegated-dependency OR (provenance=inherited-constrained AND pin facts > 1) OR (provenance=native-first-party AND AGIL-3/6 = yes) OR provenance=inherited-platform OR (provenance=inherited-constrained AND pin facts == 1)))
overall < 50 OR any clock item satisfies provenance=native-first-party AND (AGIL-1 or AGIL-2 or AGIL-6 = no)

bucket_override.when: overall >= 80 AND any clock_item has blast_radius=fleet AND provenance=native-first-party AND (AGIL-1 or AGIL-2 or AGIL-6 = no)

fips_interaction._comment: Plan v1.3 section 4.7 — conditional, never a blanket blocker. When fips_mode=true appears on facts, apply these rules per-provider to determine effective PQC posture under FIPS constraints.

rules.when: fips_mode=true AND provider's PQC algorithms are NOT yet in its FIPS-validated module (see provider_fips_pqc_notes)
fips_mode=true AND provider version is below PQC minimum even without FIPS
fips_mode=true AND provider's FIPS-validated module includes PQC algorithms
fips_mode=true AND third-party PQC library (liboqs, oqs-provider, circl) — not covered by the platform FIPS module

provider_fips_pqc_notes._comment: Per-provider guidance for the agent to reason about FIPS×PQC interaction. These are reasoning aids, not hardcoded thresholds — verify against current certification status.
provider_fips_pqc_notes.go: Go 1.24+: ML-KEM (FIPS 203) IS CMVP-validated in Go's crypto/internal/fips140 module, and X25519MLKEM768 is allowed under GODEBUG=fips140=on. However, X25519MLKEM768 has no CMVP certificate for the hybrid combination itself — strict auditors (banking, federal) may reject it because X25519 lacks standalone CMVP standing as a hybrid KEM component. Go >= 1.26: SecP256r1MLKEM768 and SecP384r1MLKEM1024 use NIST curves with clear CMVP lineage — prefer these for regulated environments.
provider_fips_pqc_notes.openssl: OpenSSL 3.5+: ML-KEM is implemented but FIPS provider certification for PQC is separate from the base module cert. Check whether the specific FIPS provider build (e.g., RHEL's openssl-fips-provider RPM) has PQC in its validated algorithm list.
provider_fips_pqc_notes.jdk: JDK 24+: ML-KEM (JEP 496) and ML-DSA (JEP 497) are javax.crypto APIs only — NOT TLS key exchange. TLS hybrid KEX (JEP 527) defaults in JDK 27. JCE FIPS providers (e.g., BC-FIPS, Amazon Corretto Crypto) may not yet include PQC in their FIPS-validated boundary. Check the provider's CMVP certificate.
provider_fips_pqc_notes.node: Node.js uses OpenSSL under the hood — FIPS posture follows the linked OpenSSL FIPS provider. If --enable-fips or --force-fips is active, PQC availability depends on whether the OpenSSL FIPS provider cert covers ML-KEM.
provider_fips_pqc_notes.rustls: Rust with aws-lc-rs (fips feature): PQC support depends on the aws-lc-fips module version and its CMVP certificate. ring does not support FIPS. Native rustls has no FIPS mode. NOTE: Rust apps using the `openssl` crate (reqwest with native-tls, actix-web with openssl feature) follow system OpenSSL FIPS posture instead — see openssl entry.
provider_fips_pqc_notes.gnutls: GnuTLS FIPS mode restricts to FIPS-approved algorithms. PQC (ML-KEM) support is experimental and unlikely to be in the FIPS module boundary yet.
provider_fips_pqc_notes.nss: NSS FIPS mode: check the specific NSS FIPS module version for PQC algorithm inclusion.

pqc_classification_map._comment: usage (from ir8547-mapping.json rule_map) + clock -> per-finding pqc_classification for report.schema.json.

server_side_caveat._comment: Infrastructure-governed decision points cannot claim PQC on client toolchain alone.

rules.when: governance=infrastructure AND no runtime_evidence for this endpoint
governance=infrastructure AND provider openssl < 3.5 in base image or known server version lacks ML-KEM support
